title: eps, v-prediction and flow: how a model's output is read
hook: The same network output means different things to different models. model_sampling.py is where ComfyUI says which, and what happens when it says wrong.

verified.claim: The conversions in the lab are copied from EPS, V_PREDICTION and CONST.
Real calculate_denoised gives the values the lab's formulas give: at sigma 3, input 2, output 0.5, eps 0.5 and v -0.27434.
verified.ref: comfy.model_sampling classes in a Python session

verified.claim: With zsnr the real sigma_max is 4518.76, with sigma_min 0.02917.
percent_to_sigma(0.5) is 1.6156 on the SD table and 0.75 on a flow model with shift 3.
ModelSamplingSD3 and ModelSamplingFlux compute their shift as in the lab.

unchecked: We read only the abstract of Salimans and Ho (2022). The v formula here comes from ComfyUI's code and the lab's check, not from their text.
We did not render an eps model loaded as v or the other way round. The lab shows the size of the error in the clean-latent estimate on perfect outputs, not what a real picture looks like.
